suggestions: reorder joins to reduce intermediate rows
pre-filter a large table as a CTE before the join
optimized_sql:
SELECT s.s_store_name,
       s.s_company_id,
       s.s_street_number,
       s.s_street_name,
       s.s_street_type,
       s.s_suite_number,
       s.s_city,
       s.s_county,
       s.s_state,
       s.s_zip,
       agg."30 days" AS "30 days",
       agg."31-60 days" AS "31-60 days",
       agg."61-90 days" AS "61-90 days",
       agg."91-120 days" AS "91-120 days",
       agg.">120 days" AS ">120 days"
FROM (
    SELECT ss.ss_store_sk,
           SUM(CASE WHEN (sr.sr_returned_date_sk - ss.ss_sold_date_sk <= 30) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS "30 days",
           SUM(CASE WHEN (sr.sr_returned_date_sk - ss.ss_sold_date_sk > 30) AND (sr.sr_returned_date_sk - ss.ss_sold_date_sk <= 60) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS "31-60 days",
           SUM(CASE WHEN (sr.sr_returned_date_sk - ss.ss_sold_date_sk > 60) AND (sr.sr_returned_date_sk - ss.ss_sold_date_sk <= 90) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS "61-90 days",
           SUM(CASE WHEN (sr.sr_returned_date_sk - ss.ss_sold_date_sk > 90) AND (sr.sr_returned_date_sk - ss.ss_sold_date_sk <= 120) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS "91-120 days",
           SUM(CASE WHEN (sr.sr_returned_date_sk - ss.ss_sold_date_sk > 120) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS ">120 days"
    FROM (
        SELECT sr_ticket_number, sr_item_sk, sr_customer_sk, sr_returned_date_sk
        FROM store_returns
        WHERE sr_returned_date_sk IN (SELECT d2.d_date_sk FROM date_dim d2 WHERE d2.d_year = 2001 AND d2.d_moy = 8)
    ) AS sr
    JOIN store_sales ss
      ON ss.ss_ticket_number = sr.sr_ticket_number
     AND ss.ss_item_sk = sr.sr_item_sk
    WHERE ss.ss_customer_sk = sr.sr_customer_sk
    GROUP BY ss.ss_store_sk
) AS agg
JOIN store s ON s.s_store_sk = agg.ss_store_sk
ORDER BY s.s_store_name, s.s_company_id, s.s_street_number, s.s_street_name, s.s_street_type, s.s_suite_number, s.s_city, s.s_county, s.s_state, s.s_zip
LIMIT 100

reasoning_trace:
1. SEMI-JOIN PUSHDOWN + INDEX ACCESS — TARGET: store_returns.sr_returned_date_sk ↔ date_dim d2 (sr_returned_date_sk = d2.d_date_sk) — TRANSFORMATION: restrict store_returns to only the d_date_sk values where d_year=2001 and d_moy=8, using an index on sr_returned_date_sk, so only August-2001 returns are joined to store_sales.

2. REVERSE JOIN ORDER / INDEX PROBE — TARGET: store_sales ↔ store_returns join (ss_ticket_number = sr_ticket_number AND ss_item_sk = sr_item_sk AND ss_customer_sk = sr_customer_sk) — TRANSFORMATION: drive from the small filtered store_returns set and probe store_sales by its primary key (ss_ticket_number, ss_item_sk), then filter ss_customer_sk, avoiding a full scan of all 57.6M store_sales rows.

3. ELIMINATE REDUNDANT DIMENSION JOIN — TARGET: date_dim d1 (ss_sold_date_sk = d1.d_date_sk) — TRANSFORMATION: remove the d1 join entirely because no d1 column is selected or filtered; it only adds an unnecessary join to store_sales.

4. PUSH AGGREGATION BEFORE STORE DIMENSION — TARGET: GROUP BY s_store_name, s_company_id, s_street_number, ..., s_zip and the store join — TRANSFORMATION: compute the five conditional sums grouping only by ss_store_sk (and the return-age bucket logic), then join store afterwards to project the 10 display columns, shrinking the grouping key from 10 wide columns to one store key.
